transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-21 16:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Park (Redwood AE), Devon Kim (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Cosmos CTO), Maya Chen (Cosmos Senior ML Eng), Liam O'Connor (Cosmos Head of Infra)
Recording link: zoom.us/recap/xxx (shared in notes)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Cosmos's use case for embeddings + reranking. Main concerns: throughput for 10M+ docs, vector DB integration strategy (OpenSearch vs managed vector DB), embedding dimensionality (512 vs 1536), hybrid search with BM25, and which Redwood deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) fits their security and latency requirements. Action items and next steps agreed at end.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain: slow relevance and search latency, inconsistent rerank quality
- Index size: planning 10M documents initially, vector dims 1536 with later experiments at 768
- Throughput target: 50-200 qps, sub-200ms rerank step goal for host-side scoring
- Vector DB options: OpenSearch plugin, Pinecone trial, self-hosted Milvus/Faiss on infra
- Deployment preference: start Hosted POC, evaluate Dedicated for production, Private for data residency
- Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, VPC peering, KMS key control

Transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro, im alyssa park from Redwood, with me is devon our solutions engineer, you each want to intro quick?
[00:06] Raj: hi im raj, cto at cosmos, we run a clinical knowledge platform, we ingest papers, notes, and internal policies ~10 to 20 million docs ongoing, main goal is better QA retrieval and a reranker for search results.
[00:20] Maya: maya here, i own the embedding infra and rerank experiments, today we want to figure out integration patterns and cost/throughput tradeoffs.
[00:30] Liam: liam, infra, interested in networking, vpc, and how to run low-latency queries from our EU and US regions.
[00:37] Devon: thanks, cool, we'll aim to cover architecture options, throughput, and a POC plan, feel free to interrupt.

[03:05] Devon: first question, what's your current retrieval stack? you mentioned elasticsearch before?
[03:12] Raj: yeah we have an opensearch cluster running BM25, with a bit of custom scoring, embeddings are currently experimental; we spun up a faiss service in k8s but its maintenance is a pain, and indexing at 10M killed memory.
[03:30] Alyssa: that tracks, a lot of teams hit faiss memory/ops at that scale, question for maya, what embedding model dims are you using?
[03:40] Maya: prototype used a 768-d model (open model), but for clinical we think 1536 gives better quality. concern is index size and storage cost, also whether to store dense vectors in our DB or push to a managed vector DB.

[05:15] Devon: two patterns: 1) host embeddings in managed vector DB (pinecone/milvus) and call reranker at query time, or 2) keep dense vectors in S3/own store + use Redwood to host reranker and do on-the-fly embed + ANN search via our runtime. hybrid search is common: bm25 to narrow candidates then vector rerank.
[05:45] Raj: hybrid is exactly what we want — bm25 first, then 100 candidate rerank with a light cross-encoder. main asks: how do you handle throughput? if we need 100 qps with 200ms budget for rerank that's tight.
[06:05] Devon: okay, couple levers: candidate set size, dimensionality, and batch scoring. On Redwood Hosted you can get multi-threaded batching and streaming; Dedicated offers pinned GPU pools for predictable throughput — for cross-encoder style rerank (300-500 tokens), we see X qps on a dedicated instance, for exact numbers we can run a benchmark.
[06:35] Maya: can you give an order of magnitude? like 50 qps per GPU or 200 qps?
[06:42] Devon: rough numbers: for a 1k-parameter cross-encoder at 1536 dims if you're doing just vector dot and a small transformer rerank, on a dedicated V100/80-ish GPU you might get 100-300 single-thread qps with batching; with our batching and quantized kernels it can be higher. caveat: cross-encoders are heavier. Many customers do vector-first to reduce candidates to 50-100 then rerank.

[08:00] Liam: infrastructure question — if we do Dedicated, do we need VPC peering or does Redwood provide private networking? also KMS for key control?
[08:10] Alyssa: Dedicated runs in isolated pools; we offer VPC peering and private endpoints for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Private (on-prem or customer VPC) you get full control including KMS/HSM integrations. We can share SOC2 and our network diagrams.

[09:12] Raj: how about the vector DB integration — if we keep opensearch, what does integration look like?
[09:20] Devon: we integrate with OpenSearch's vector plugin commonly. Pattern: index chunks with BM25 fields + vector field, use a hybrid query combining BM25 score + vector score. Alternatively, store vectors in Pinecone or Milvus and return candidate ids to be fetched and reranked. Each approach has tradeoffs: OpenSearch keeps locality and simpler infra but may not match HNSW performance of Milvus; Pinecone is simple but costed.
[09:56] Maya: ops wise, we want low maintenance. Pinecone looked attractive but licensing and data residency is a concern. If we self-host Milvus, we fear operational overhead.

[11:10] Devon: that's common; a lot of teams start with Pinecone or Hosted simple flows, then move to Dedicated + managed Milvus on customer's cloud, or use Redwood Private when data residency requires on-prem. POC suggestion: start Hosted + Pinecone for speed of experiment then test Dedicated with Milvus for scale/latency.

[12:05] Raj: can Redwood host the embeddings computation too? like batch embedding jobs?
[12:12] Alyssa: yes, Redwood API supports embeddings (we have model catalog). We can host embedding generation and store vectors in your chosen DB, or you can generate offline and upload. Many customers use Redwood's embeddings to ensure consistent vectors and then serve via Pinecone/Milvus.

[13:30] Maya: embedding dimension concern again — storage: 10M docs * 1536 dims * 4 bytes ~ 61GB? wait, that's wrong math — can you walk through?
[13:45] Devon: quick calc: 10M * 1536 * 4 bytes = ~61,440,000,000 bytes = ~57.2 GiB — actually it's 61.44 GB (raw), plus index overhead for HNSW maybe 2-3x depending on ef/construction. So plan for 200GB regionally. If you quantize to 2 bytes per dim (int8/float16) you reduce storage. So dimensionality and quantization matter for cost.
[14:20] Maya: ok that helps. Also curious about hybrid scoring — do you recommend BM25 first and then vector rerank or fuse scores?
[14:30] Devon: both. BM25-first to narrow is cheaper; fused scoring (weighted sum BM25 + vector sim) can boost recall. Operationally BM25-first then rerank with a cross-encoder often gives best end-user quality with acceptable cost.

[16:05] Raj: SLA and latency commitments — Hosted has soft SLOs, but for production we need predictable p99 latency. Does Dedicated provide SLOs?
[16:15] Alyssa: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, committed throughput with reserved capacity. Private gives you full control and you run it on your infra so p99 is your control. We'll surface p99 numbers in the Dedicated sizing doc.

[17:10] Maya: for rerank, we plan to do 2-stage: vector recall top-500, then light cross-encoder on 50. How much does that cost? per-request cost?
[17:24] Devon: costs depend on candidate size and model choice. We'll provide a cost model in the pricing sheet — rough example: vector-only scoring w/ HNSW is cheap per request, cross-encoder is the heavy part and often the driver of per-request compute. Dedicated helps amortize that.

[19:00] Liam: question on throughput from multi-region — do you replicate indexes or route queries cross-region?
[19:10] Devon: options: replicate vector indexes regionally for low-latency queries, or route to closest region with async fallback. Dedicated supports regional pools and automated routing. Replication cost vs latency tradeoff needs sizing.

[21:40] Maya: security — can we get SSO and audit logs for embeddings access?
[21:47] Alyssa: yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. For Private you can put audit logs into your SIEM via our connector. We'll attach our security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, network diagrams).

[24:05] Raj: ok this feels good. For POC timeline what would you recommend? 2-4 weeks?
[24:12] Devon: typical POC: week 0-1: data prep and sample import (10k docs), week 2: run benchmarks (latency/throughput) and tune HNSW params, week 3: qualitative eval + rerank tuning, week 4: decision point and scale planning. So 3-4 weeks if sample data ready.

[26:30] Maya: when you benchmark can you include efConstruction/efSearch settings, M and index size? we need recommended HNSW settings for 1536 dims and 10M scale.
[26:40] Devon: yes, we'll include recommended HNSW params and example memory/latency tradeoffs. Also run with int8 quantized vectors to show storage savings.

[28:00] Raj: any gotchas switching from our current opensearch BM25-first approach?
[28:07] Devon: migration common issues: chunking strategy (how you split docs affects recall), embedding drift across models, and cold-start for indexes. We'll help with chunking heuristics and provide eval harness.

[30:15] Maya: internal question, we have PHI in some docs, can Redwood avoid seeing raw text?
[30:23] Alyssa: Hosted processes text in our environment; if PHI is a concern we'd recommend Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment. You can also encrypt payloads and use customer-managed keys. We'll surface exact data flow diagrams in the security pack.

[33:00] Liam: ops question — if we self-host Milvus, does Redwood still integrate for rerank?
[33:07] Devon: yes, we can call your Milvus endpoints; pattern: you return candidate ids, send candidate text or embeddings to Redwood runtime for rerank. We can also host the rerank near the vector DB via Private/Dedicated collocation to reduce cross-cloud hops.

[36:20] Raj: ok, are there customers in healthcare doing similar?
[36:26] Alyssa: yes, a couple — we can share anonymized case studies where customers used Dedicated + Milvus for 20M docs with ~150 qps and reached p99 below 300ms for rerank. We'll include references.

[38:40] Maya: one last thing — evaluation metrics: we want precision@10, nDCG, and human evals, can Redwood help instrument that?
[38:48] Devon: absolutely, we have an eval harness and quality monitoring in Redwood Optimize that can run regression tests, attach prompt sets, and alert on quality regressions. We'll include sample dashboards.

[41:10] Alyssa: recap and next steps: we'll send pricing + Dedicated sizing, Devon will send benchmarking template + HNSW suggestions, Maya to share 10k sample, propose POC kickoff next monday 2027-02-28 for a deeper scoping with infra.
[41:28] Raj: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[41:33] Liam: thanks, appreciate it.
[41:35] Maya: thanks.

[45:50] Alyssa: closing — notes and action items will be in follow-up email, i'll add links to security pack and sample pricing. Bye.

End of transcript.
